_comment: Where step 10 (pipeline/10-figures.py) looks for figures, and the licence each source states (checked on each source's own site, docs/FIGURES-PLAN.md section 2). Only CC BY 4.0 or public-domain images are used. Every request goes through pipeline/_http.py (cached under data/, throttled, descriptive user agent). Servier is read from its category listing pages, page by page; its search is disallowed by robots.txt and is not used. NIH BioArt Source has no listing that works without its JavaScript application, so step 10 checks a pinned list of entries (found by searching the site's pages for our structures' names); each entry's own title must still equal one of our names, and its own licence field must say Public Domain or CC BY.

hgnc.name: HGNC (HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee)
hgnc._note: Not a figure source. For a cell type's HPA image, step 10 prefers a protein that HRA's ASCT+B tables list as a biomarker of that cell type. The tables name biomarkers by HGNC id and HPA by Ensembl gene id, so step 10 reads HGNC's own record of each such id (its ensembl_gene_id, for an approved symbol) to join the two. Some rows give a biomarker another gene's id, so a row counts only where HGNC's record also carries one of the names the row gives that biomarker (its symbol, approved name, a previous symbol or an alias, ignoring case, spaces and punctuation). Nothing from HGNC is shown. HGNC's terms (genenames.org/about): its data are freely available to all; it asks to be credited as the HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee at the University of Cambridge, with its website URL.
hgnc.credit: HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee at the University of Cambridge, https://www.genenames.org (RRID:SCR_002827)

bioart.name: NIH BioArt Source (NIAID)
bioart._note: No entries are pinned. Entry pages found by web search (bioart/50, 111, 112, 114, 141, 253, 313, 356; November 2026) give a title, a licence field (Public Domain) and image links, but every image file they link (nih3d-v2-data-cln-media-prod.s3.amazonaws.com) answers HTTP 403 to a direct request: the files are served only to the site's own pages, so Bio Map does not use them. Step 10 still reads any entry listed here and reports one whose image cannot be downloaded.

grays.name: Gray's Anatomy (1918)
grays._note: A last resort (decision 1, approved): only for bones, muscles, vessels and nerves (an atlas structure under one of `classes` in FMA: bone organ, muscle organ, segment of vascular tree organ, nerve), never for tissues, cells or organelles, and only where no other source has a figure. A plate matches when its own legend title, the text before the legend's first period in the scan's OCR, is one of the structure's names. The plate is cropped from the scan's page image (the Internet Archive's BookReader JPEG, cropped locally with sharp), between the nearest line of text above it and its legend. The 1918 edition is in the public domain in the United States by date; its editor W. H. Lewis died in 1964, so plates he added may still be in copyright elsewhere.
grays.caption: Historical illustration (Gray’s Anatomy, 1918). Some labels use older names.
grays.citation: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed., edited by Lewis WH. Philadelphia: Lea & Febiger, 1918.
grays.rights: Public domain in the United States (published 1918). Scan: Internet Archive, digitized by Brigham Young University, Harold B. Lee Library.
